item.description: PITTSBURGH — From talking smack to being body-slammed, Browns defensive end Jared Verse has had the complete professional wrestling experience with the Pittsburgh Steelers . Needless to say, Verse did not appreciate the move Steelers guard Mason McCormick executed against him in the first quarter of Cleveland's 27-6 loss on Sunday, Nov. 1, at Acrisure Stadium. "I love football. I love the aggression," Verse said. "I love how much power goes into it, how much people put into their lives into football. But to do something like that, I just, I can't have respect for anything like that." "I had jumped in the air to try to block the kick," Verse said. "He sweeped my legs in the air. Ended up landing on my head. That's football. I mean, I'm very upset about it. And, obviously, you know, if this wasn't football, I would have reacted a different way." Verse took some solace in McCormick receiving a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty. item.title: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat from Patriots vs. Dolphins
item.description: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England Patriots are back in the win column. Taking on the Dolphins in a rainy Miami on Sunday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel secured a 24-19 victory to improve to 5-3 on the season. It wasn’t a groundbreaking performance, but one that still allowed the team to head back to Foxborough with some momentum on its side. With that said, let’s dive into our breakdown of the good and the not-so-good from the win at Hard Rock Stadium. The good: Halftime adjustments Judged by the game’s first 30 minutes, the Patriots did not look like a team capable of competing for a playoff spot this year. Despite going up against a one-win team, they were outperformed and found themselves trailing by 10 points heading into the half. Coming out of it, however, they showed some much-needed signs of life. The inconsistency that plagued them early on, especially on offense but also in parts on the defensive side of the ball, became a thing of the past — partially due to improved performance, partially due to some apparent tweaks being made. At first glance, inserting Ben Brown at left guard in place of Walter Rouse and being more aggressive with the man coverage calls seemed to factor into the change. Whatever it was, the Patriots showed more urgency and the results looked the part. The offense in particular did a 180 after being stuck in the mud in the first two quarters: it starting pushing the ball downfield in the passing game and finished drives with touchdowns. After going three-and-out to open the second half, the unit fournd the end zone on three straight possessions to start pulling away. Whatever buttons Mike Vrabel and company pushed during the intermission, it worked. The bad: Procedural issues The Patriots looked uncharacteristically sloppy on Sunday, and one number that reflects this is this: six — that’s the number of pre-snap penalties the team had. On offense, rookie tight end Eli Raridon was flagged for a pair of false starts. On defense, Joshua Farmer, Gabe Jacas, Dre’Mont Jones and Cory Durden were all penalized for lining up offsides; Jones’ infraction negated an interception by teammate Christian Elliss. In addition, the Patriots were flagged two more times for a grand total of eight penalties, and a loss of 46 yards. In the grand scheme of things, those issues were a footnote. That’s partially due to the Dolphins not being good enough overall to challenge New England even with the aided penalty yardage. Other clubs, including the Green Bay Packers next Sunday, appear to be better equipped to capitalize on miscues such as these. item.title: North Carolina lands elite 2028 QB Levi Kerr after back-to-back visits to Chapel Hill
item.description: North Carolina has landed a major commitment at quarterback in the 2028 class. Elite signal-caller Levi Kerr has committed to Bill Belichick and the Tar Heels following back-to-back weekend visits to Chapel Hill. Kerr entered the final stretch of his recruitment with Michigan , Mississippi State and North Carolina on relatively equal footing, with some buzz around the Wolverines, but the Tar Heels separated themselves over the past two weeks. Kerr spent Saturday and Sunday in Chapel Hill each of the past two weekends. Those trips gave him an extended look at the program, its people and his potential future. By the end of the first weekend, Kerr knew where he wanted to play college football. “I knew last weekend when I left,” Kerr told Rivals. He returned this weekend to make sure. The third overall visit to North Carolina confirmed what he had already begun to feel. The Tar Heels rolled out the red carpet, made Kerr a priority and convinced him that Chapel Hill was home. “It felt like family. From the coaching staff to the people working inside the football offices, I felt comfortable with everyone.” That connection mattered throughout his decision-making process. Kerr wanted to find a program where he could build lasting relationships, trust the people around him and feel comfortable away from football. North Carolina checked those boxes. “I got to stay close to home and that was always something for me,” he said. “The combination of that, what the staff is doing and the education being second to none — that is why I chose North Carolina.” Kerr has been impressed by the progress North Carolina is making under Belichick. He has watched the Tar Heels develop their young players, build the roster and establish a foundation for the future. The number of freshmen contributing this season caught his attention, along with the work the coaching staff has put into developing the team. Kerr believes North Carolina is moving in the right direction. “Belichick is one of the best to ever do it. It doesn’t get any better than Belichick. One of the best of all time.” He was wanted by Belichick. During his visits, he repeatedly saw his name at the top of the program’s recruiting board. It was a clear message about how highly the staff valued him. “I saw my name at the top of their board four times,” Kerr said. That attention reinforced what the coaches had been telling him throughout the process. North Carolina wanted Kerr to lead its 2028 class at quarterback, and the staff made sure he understood his importance to the program. The first of his back-to-back weekend visits changed the direction of his recruitment. He left Chapel Hill with North Carolina in front and returned knowing a commitment could be coming. The second weekend sealed it. Now, his recruitment is over. “I’m done,” Kerr said.

item.title: Alex Eala has been handed a silver lining despite her recent loss at the Tokyo Open
item.description: Alex Eala has been given some significant encouragement, despite losing in the quarter-finals of the Tokyo Open. Eala has enjoyed her best ever season in 2026 , having won her first WTA title at the Washington Open , reached the fourth round of Wimbledon and broke into the top 20. However, the Filipina has struggled to continue this form since the US Open , with Eala winning just three of her seven WTA Tour matches since the last Grand Slam of the year. Two of Eala’s losses have come against Diana Shnaider , including at the Tokyo Open , but what has happened since then should provide her with a huge morale boost. Alex Eala pushed eventual champion Diana Shnaider the most at the Tokyo Open Eala lost to Shnaider at both the Ningbo Open and the Tokyo Open, but their most recent encounter in the Japanese capital was much closer fought as the Russian came from a set down to win 2-6, 7-6(5), 6-4. Shnaider would go on to win the Tokyo Open title, her first tournament victory of the 2026 season, after beating Leylah Fernandez in the final. Eala was not the only player to push Shnaider to three sets, but she was certainly the closest to beating her, having been just two points away from a straight sets win. This should be hugely encouraging for Eala, not only because she had been through a run of relatively disappointing results, but also because she closed the gap on Shnaider. It goes to show the margins between a player losing in the quarter-finals and another winning the title, showing that the Tokyo Open was definitely Eala’s best tournament since the US Open. item.description: The Los Angeles Rams got the win they needed against the Chargers in the “Battle for LA”, and not much else. This is the NFL. You cannot set the bar at a blowout even against the bottom feeders of the league, which the Chargers are at now 0-7. The Rams also did little to inspire confidence moving forward as the schedule grows more difficult. The offense feels disjointed and untalented. The defense was stifling, although Justin Herbert may as well have worn royal and sol for as often as he gave the ball to the Rams. Most importantly, the mission was accomplished. The Rams are now 4-4 and have dug themselves out of the hole they put themselves in amid early season struggles. Two very winnable games are on the horizon against the Washington Commanders and the Arizona Cardinals. Keep stacking boxes and LA could soon find themselves at 6-4. But before we turn the page, let’s revisit the individual contributions that made the difference in the win over the Chargers. Winners Blake Corum & the run game The offense goes as Blake Corum does. For most of the season the Rams have searched for a spark plug on offense, and the answer may have been right in front of our eyes this whole time. When Corum is involved and productive, the offense operates at the highest levels we’ve seen from them so far. Corum rushed 11 times for 73 yards (6.6 average), including a 23-yard touchdown that flipped the momentum in the third quarter. Kyren Williams added a less efficient 16 carries for 56 yards (3.5 average) with a short touchdown, although his average was hurt by closing out the game late into the fourth quarter. This is always worth mentioning: anytime two running backs produce, you must give credit to the offensive line. Matthew Stafford was sacked only a single time. item.title: 2026 D-backs Prospect All-Stars: Reliever of the Year
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 13: Joe Ariola #52 of the Arizona Diamondbacks pitches during a game between the Salt River Rafters and the Glendale Desert Dogs at Camelback Ranch on October 13, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Introduction There are some real issues that arise when talking about relief pitching prospects, and I think it’s important we discuss them before actually highlighting the best 2026 seasons by relievers in the Diamondbacks farm system. If you’ve been around this game long enough, you’ll eventually hear a casual fan suggest a team fix their bullpen through the draft, or that they should use their first pick in a draft on some dominant college reliever. Even in the weakest, shallowest of drafts, this is viewed as a bad idea because you’re almost always going to be leaving better players on the board. The last time the Dbacks drafted a reliever with their first round pick was when they selected reliever Dan Schlereth with the 26th overall pick in the 2008 draft, while much more notable pitchers like Gerrit Cole, Jake Odorizzi, and Craig Kimbrel, and hitters like Dee Strange-Gordon and Charlie Blackmon were still on the board. The list of successful early draft picks spent on amateur relief pitchers that then went on to become successful relievers in the Major Leagues is an incredibly short one, headlined by such notable names as Gregg Olson and Paul Shuey. This adds to the rarity of seeing a pitcher who is explicitly a reliever at the top of top prospect list unless they have overwhelming velocity. All of the dominant relievers you can think of are almost certainly a former starting pitcher who at some point in his professional career was converted to relief. Aside from that, we have the real issue of how are we defining what does and does not count as a reliever?” If we exclude any pitchers who started a game, that leaves out pitchers who operated as openers but were no different in usage than any other relief pitcher. For the purposes of this article, I’m defining a reliever as a pitcher who did not start a game outside of being an opener, which would be a start with less than two innings pitched. If we just used examples of guys who are likely to be converted to relief or whom I think should be converted to relief we will be hear all day, so instead, we are going for the much more narrower definition. item.title: The Perfect Role Player
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 03: Dustin Harris #29 of the San Diego Padres hits a single against the Milwaukee Brewers during the ninth inning in game one of the National League Division Series at American Family Field on October 03, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). The Perfect Role Player Prior to joining the Padres, Dustin Harris had played in just 38 MLB games. Most of that time came with the Texas Rangers (21 games) before playing parts of 2026 with the Chicago White Sox and Houston Astros. Harris was released in early August before the Friars scooped him up on a minor-league deal with San Diego. The longtime minor-leaguer had struggled to break through despite a .289/.377/.457 career slash line in the minors. His big-league breakout came the second he joined the brown and gold. Overall Grade: A+ In 29 games with Triple-A El Paso, Harris batted .350/.422/.617 with six homers and a 1.039 OPS. That earned him a promotion to the big-league club. He promptly earned the starting left field job, but still platooned with Samad Taylor on occasion. In 28 games with San Diego, Harris batted .322 with a .422 slugging percentage. His lack of walks (5 BB) or power (0 HR) make him an intriguing option for left field in 2027. However, for the time that Harris spent with San Diego, he was phenomenal. He knocked in 14 runners and scored 18 runs of his own all in just 90 at-bats. With that small sample in mind, Harris was one of the best role players in all of baseball for the 2026 season. There was certainly some luck involved in Harris’ production. His .278 xBA was a good deal lower than his actual .322 batting average. There’s a question of whether Harris will be able to replicate his breakout performance in 2027. However, the Padres will certainly give him the opportunity to earn the left field spot in Spring Training. Harris could be an invaluable part of San Diego’s roster for the coming years if he can build on his success.

item.description: 4 stats that show how bad Chargers' Justin Herbert has been in 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There is plenty of blame to go around for the Chargers ' 0-7 start, but there is no doubt it's been an ugly year for Justin Herbert. The former Pro-Bowler's numbers speak for themselves, as he has double the interceptions as he has passing touchdowns, and there just haven's been any clean games for L.A.'s offense. As offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job comes into question, these stats show Herbert has to receive some of the blame. MORE: Why Steelers can run away with AFC North 4 stats that show how bad Justin Herbert has been in 2026 9 consecutive starts without multiple TDs Dating back to 2025, Herbert now has a streak of nine consecutive starts without multiple touchdowns, a streak that only Ryan Leaf (12) has beaten in Chargers history. For a quarterback who was hailed as one of the NFL's best in the early years of his career, it's a baffling stat. It's not uncommon for high-level quarterbacks to be turnover-prone, but they at least rack up touchdowns right alongside those turnovers. Herbert doesn't have a single game with more than one touchdown this season, and the streak is already longer than any Philip Rivers ever had. As many INTs as 2023 and 2024 combined Herbert has thrown 10 touchdowns in seven games this season, matching his combined interception total from 2023 and 2024. That's as absurd as it sounds: Herbert threw exactly 10 interceptions across 30 games between those seasons, and he now has 10 interceptions in just seven games this season. Chargers fans would've hoped 10 interceptions in seven from Herbert would at least mean he is putting up gaudy numbers from a yards and touchdowns standpoint, but that hasn't been the case. MORE: Why Ravens' Super Bowl hopes are doomed with Lamar Jackson injury Only QB with an INT in each game in 2026 Herbert is the only NFL quarterback with an interception in each of his team's games this season, despite playing one fewer game than teams who haven't reached their bye. The Chargers have been looking for a clean game from Herbert to get him back on track, but it hasn't come to this point. 4th QB in NFL history to start 0-7 with an INT in each game With Sunday's loss to the Rams , Herbert became the fourth quarterback in NFL history to start the season with an interception and a loss in each of his first seven games. The club Herbert joined is nothing to be excited about, as it's comprised of Steve DeBerg (1985), Dennis Shaw (1971) and Norm Snead (1961). McDaniel's offense has been all-around abysmal through two months, and Herbert has now entered conversations including the name Steve DeBerg after rivaling the production of some of the NFL's elite quarterbacks in his early years. item.title: Cowboys players back coach Brian Schottenheimer as questions about his future amplify
item.description: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer calls a play during the first half of an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Arlington. (Elías Valverde II/The Dallas Morning News) ARLINGTON — Cowboys owner Jerry Jones swatted down multiple questions about the status of head coach Brian Schottenheimer with a similar response after the Cowboys fell to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, 33-30 . “That’s not in my mind at this time," he said about changing coaches. "The thing that’s in my mind: we tee it up in those kinds of spots to win it.” That didn't happen on Sunday. Wins have eluded the Cowboys more times than not under Schottenheimer. Dallas is now 3-5 this season. Schottenheimer is now 10-14-1. His .420 winning percentage is lower than every coach in Cowboys' history aside from Dave Campo, who was fired after three full seasons. It's why the questions about the future under Schottenheimer will persist externally until change happens. Cowboys players fielded some of those questions about Schottenheimer on Sunday, too. "I've got full confidence in all my coaches," Cowboys defensive tackle Kenny Clark said. "I think they do a good job of putting a great plan together. It's on players out there to execute. That's all I got to say about that." Multiple players agreed. Cowboys left guard Tyler Smith also pointed to the execution needing to be improved. Outside linebacker Von Miller — the oldest player on the Cowboys and a Super Bowl champion — compared coaching to parenting. "Sometimes you raise your kids a certain way, and you teach them lessons, and you expect them to act a certain way when they go out. Sometimes the kids just go out there and do things that are not a reflection of who you are as a parent. And I use that reference for our coaching staff," Miller said. "We have amazing coaches. They keep us prepared, ready to go mentally, physically, emotionally. They breathe life into us, and just for whatever reason, that's the product. The product that went out there is not a reflection of our coaching staff. This is pro sports. You know, this is not -- this is not parenting. So at the end of the day, you know, the buck has to stop somewhere. Somebody's gonna get the blame." Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott made it clear that Schottenheimer shouldn't get the blame for their 3-5 record alone. “It’s all of us. Don’t put the blame on one person. I think that’s weak. I think that’s cowardly," Prescott said. "This game is about all 11 of us that touch the field and every person that has a part in it, coaches and support staff. It’s never just one person’s fault. “Don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and backing him up and one another up.” Subscribe Sign up for the Morning Roundup, a free newsletter delivering the latest North Texas news each morning. For head coach Charita Stubbs , seeing her team continue to put itself in a position to win and then letting it go is a recurring trend. It’s just like always one thing after another after an error happens. Do I think that we were not dialed in?
